behavior.statement: Every case reached the record its terminal assertion names, each produced by a press on the control the capture names, and both declared alternate paths reached theirs.

ui.statement: Carried from the surface audit at this same commit: presentation, responsive and render-truth pass; accessibility and contrast fail into the design family; taste is fix-first on two criteria that family owns. Nothing this walk saw contradicts it.

ux.statement: Mean 3.55 over the eleven criteria, down from 3.82 in run 1 because pressing rather than typing addresses exposed how the collection is reached. UX-6 gates and fails; UX-5 and UX-2 fail on the same cause, that nothing in the product links to the collection.

entries.measured: All four cases reached the terminal assertion flow.md names and both declared alternate paths reached theirs, and this time every one of the nine steps was a press on a rendered control — the sign-in form included — with no endpoint, mutation or console call standing in for one. 37.7s wide and 35.6s narrow against a 90s budget.
entries.control: every control in the walk; the presses are listed in result.json

entries.measured: Seven committed presses for the flow’s six declared steps. The overspend is entirely the way in: opening the collection is one step in flow.md and costs four presses in the product — Open workspace, Installed, View details into a module, then the Modules breadcrumb — because no surface links to the collection directly.
entries.control: the seven presses the flow itself needed, counted from steps/

entries.measured: A wrong password kept the form, kept the email and left the password editable; "That email or password is not right." rendered 52px below the password field rather than as a summary at the top; the correction was made at that field and the flow reached its terminal assertion one press later.

The Sign in control changed within 0ms of the press, measured on the control itself. No step outlasted one second, so the progress and escape cases never fired, and no signal claimed a settlement the store had not confirmed.

The collection is reachable from no navigation surface in the product. The workspace page carries seven segments, zero anchors and never uses the word Modules; the only control anywhere that leads to the collection is the breadcrumb inside a module workspace, so a person must already have opened a module to find the list of modules. Measured at four presses from entry against the two levels the console band allows.
entries.control: AgentOSSolutionModulePage>Breadcrumbs>Step[Modules]; no other control in the product reaches the collection

entries.measured: The refused installed list offers its own Try again, and the walk pressed it and watched that section come back while the others stayed as they were. The second refusal does not: a module the workspace does not own says "The server refused this installation or workspace identity." and the region holds no control at all — zero anchors, zero buttons. Only the surrounding console navigation leads out. That screen is in the installed module workspace this mission held unchanged.
entries.control: AgentOSSolutionModuleLedger>SurfaceCard[installed]>EmptyNotice>Button[Try again] for the refusal that recovers; the not-owned refusal offers no control at all

entries.measured: Reloading Diagnostics returned Diagnostics selected under the same heading; back returned Setup, the step before it, with nothing re-committed; every mid-flow address opened directly and resumed there.
entries.control: AgentOSSolutionModulePage>RouteTabs>Tab[Diagnostics], then the browser reload and back

entries.measured: Email and Password carry persistent visible labels rather than placeholders standing in for them; the rejection renders beside the password field and stays while it is corrected; Tab from Email lands on Password and Enter submits from the field; the fields declare autocomplete email and current-password with an email input mode.

At 390x844 the step primary Create module sits at y=320 of an 844px frame, in the upper half rather than the lower half or a sticky bar. It is above the fold and needs no scrolling, which is why this is a 3 rather than lower, but a thumb crosses the frame to reach it.

Create module carries the same verb and the same position, top right of the intro, on every render of the collection; every custom row action reads Resume interview or View module and every installed row action reads View details, one verb per consequence; the secondary pill shape is the same on every row.

Headings are nouns, controls are verbs, progress carries its unit (40% complete), and no stub copy, lorem or untranslated key appears in the application copy. But on the English surface the four catalogue cards describe themselves in Vietnamese — "Rà soát khoản phải trả, chứng từ và luồng duyệt tài chính." and three like it. That text arrives with the catalogue read rather than from the locale catalogues.
